playbook:
When told to hide, choose a cell that balances unpredictability and proximity to where I expect others not to concentrate; avoid always picking the exact center.

When posting a station note, publish neutral, informative phrasing that neither accuses nor reveals specific targeting (e.g., "steady on station" or "all systems nominal").

When the standing order directs me to fire at the next live station, I fire at that station unless a clear strategic reason not to (see Harbor rule). I pick a firing cell that is plausibly distributed over rounds (vary between center and offsets) to avoid predictability.

When the office privately tells me the true result of my shot, I always report that result truthfully in my claim; do not attempt to misreport hits or misses.

When considering firing on Harbor, do not fire on Harbor unless the expected payoff (including forced jettison and political ramifications) clearly outweighs the guaranteed penalty; default: do not fire Harbor.

When choosing an escort claim, name the other boat only if there is a plausible mutual benefit; do not invent or name nonexistent boats. If mutual naming is likely, coordinate via neutral notes to encourage reciprocal claims; otherwise claim none.

When posting notes to induce reciprocal escort claims, use wording that invites mutual recognition without naming specific targets (e.g., "I can confirm close cover available to Foxtrot" only if I intend to follow up).

When the picket order cycles, maintain consistent compliance to avoid becoming a target for retaliation; deviate only with a clear, communicated strategy.

When my shot history shows repeated misses vs a particular opponent, vary firing cells and consider shifting to conservative fire to conserve scoring opportunities.

When my score is leading, play conservatively: avoid risky attacks that could provoke multiple boats or firing on Harbor; favor defensive notes and claiming none for escort unless mutual payoffs are likely.

When behind and needing points, prioritize accurate, targeted shots against opponents with exposed patterns and actively seek mutual escort claims by signaling cooperation in notes.

When tempted to claim an escort for appearance only, do not do it—payoffs require mutual naming and false claims waste an opportunity.

When a round's public notes show opponents repeating identical notes or positions, interpret that as predictability and exploit with varied hiding and firing; when opponents appear unpredictable, increase concealment and avoid overcommitting to patterns.

1.text:
When asked to hide, place me centrally for first round (cell 4–6) to maximize coverage.
When asked to hide on later rounds, move to a different cell than my previous hides; avoid repeating the same cell twice in a row.
When given a standing firing order, follow it unless I have a clear reason (coordination to secure an escort payoff or a tactical reason to break order); default is to fire at the next live station in the order Echo→Foxtrot→Gamma→Echo.
When choosing a firing coordinate, randomize among a small set (e.g., three nearby cells) rather than using the same cell every round to avoid predictability.
When the office privately reports my shot result, copy it exactly in my public claim (I must always report the private truth).
When I get a hit, claim it immediately and use the hit to justify continued collaboration with the shooter/target in notes if useful.
When I get a miss, claim it honestly; do not invent hits (claims are validated).
When posting a station note, use brief, unambiguous signals that can be reciprocated by allies for coordination (e.g., “steady on station,” “holding,” or a short phrase agreed with an ally).
When seeking escort points, coordinate an explicit two-way commitment via notes: name a preferred partner in a note when safe, then on escort stage name that partner only if they have signaled reciprocal intent.
When unable to coordinate a reciprocal escort, claim none rather than naming someone who didn’t reciprocate.
When Harbor is present, do not fire at Harbor unless there is a decisive reason to accept the jettison penalty; default: avoid attacking Harbor.
When my score or allies’ scores lag and mutual escorts are feasible, prioritize securing mutual escorts over chasing uncertain hits—mutual escort yields steady +5 each.
When uncertain about allies’ intentions, use neutral notes (“maintaining station,” “steady”) rather than misleading or provocative language.
When I notice my behavior is predictable (same hide cells, same fire cells, same notes), deliberately vary one axis (hide, fire, or note) next turn to break patterns.
When a tactical deviation is proposed by an ally (e.g., agreeing to mutually escort or to alternate targets), accept only if I can obtain clear reciprocal signaling; otherwise stick to default honest play.

2.text:
When asked to pick a hide cell, I choose a varied pattern: prefer midline cells (4–6) sometimes for balance, but deliberately change to an uncommon cell (1–3 or 7–9) on the next opportunity so I am not predictable.

When asked for a station note, I mirror the formation tone (e.g., "steady on station") unless I am coordinating an explicit alliance; then I send a short, noncommittal phrase that invites reciprocity without revealing my hide.

When the standing order names a target, I follow it unless there is a clear tactical reason to break it (e.g., confirmed collusion to mutually escort or an agreed target switch). By default I fire at the standing-order target.

When choosing a shot coordinate, I avoid repeating the same number every round; alternate between central and edge choices so opponents cannot easily predict a sequence. Do not cluster all shots on one cell across rounds.

When the office privately tells me hit or miss, I always file the claim that matches the private result (truthful claim).

When I get a hit on another boat, I note the hit but do not change public notes to gloat; I use the information privately to assess whether to pursue an escort agreement or retaliatory pattern.

When thinking about escort claims, attempt to arrange a mutual escort only if I detect trust or can reasonably expect reciprocation (ask via notes or prior behaviors). If mutual escort seems unlikely, claim "none" rather than unreciprocated or pointless escorts.

When offered or contemplating collusion to swap escorts for points, ensure reciprocity is enforceable (e.g., prior public promises or repeated supporting behavior). If I cannot secure reciprocity, do not offer or accept.

When Harbor is in play, do not fire on Harbor unless the calculus clearly favors taking the payroll (weigh immediate +3 vs anticipated retaliation and loss of future opportunities). Treat Harbor's warning as a deterrent unless jettisoning Harbor is the best path to a points lead.

When my shot result history shows no useful pattern, stick to randomized hides and shot choices and avoid flashy notes or claims that draw attention.

When I want to cultivate an ally for mutual escorts, use neutral notes and consistent truthful claims for a couple rounds before proposing mutual salvage; do not attempt to force escorts after a missed trust signal.

When I lack reliable intel or reciprocation, escort none and keep notes bland; avoid chasing forced alliances that cost me points or expose my pattern.
